mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 5.25% over the prior 8 weeks reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, lowering the present value of expected dividends and earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% over the past 8 weeks
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the same regime are not statistically lower than during the prior 8 weeks (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 150,000 while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) remains below 4% simultaneously signals a strong labor market and disinflation, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 150,000 and UNRATE remains below 4%
regime_hint: labor market strengthening with low inflation
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative despite the signal in at least 60% of similar monthly occurrences since 2010.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly housing starts index (HOUST) exceeds 1,400 and the industrial production index (INDPRO) shows a double-digit increase, it indicates accelerating domestic demand, which is associated with higher equity valuation multiples and positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 20 consecutive months, the 5-day forward return is not statistically higher than the prior month's return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of over 10 points for three consecutive months suggests weakening supply-side constraints, which can trigger a risk-on equity premium and produce positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 10 points for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in all such 3-month episodes since 2000.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 313.5 while the federal funds rate remains below 5%, it indicates a potential shift toward inflationary pressures without aggressive tightening, which is associated with negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL 3mo avg crosses above 313.5 and FEDFUNDS < 5%
failure_condition: In 80% of similar 3-month windows since 2010, the 60-day forward return was not negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 200,000 in a month while the monthly average hourly earnings (not in the catalog, so use UNRATE instead) remains flat suggests labor market weakness that can depress equity risk premia, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 in a single month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not significantly lower than the prior month's return in at least 70% of such monthly events since 2008.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (not in the catalog - use GDPC1 as proxy for aggregate demand) above 2% y/y and a rising payrolls series (PAYEMS > 150,000) indicate robust consumer and business demand, which is predictive of positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not positive in 50% of such monthly dual-signal episodes since 2015.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to persistent supply chain resilience (indicated by a 6-month rising trend in RSAFS) is associated with lower uncertainty premia and positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns, but only when the regime is confirmed by a 2-month declining trend in inventory turnover (not in the catalog - use INDPRO as proxy).
candidate_trigger: RSAFS shows a 6-month up-trend and INDPRO shows a 2-month down-trend
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not positive in 40% of confirmed supply resilience regimes since 2018.
